extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for the Journal of Fluid Mechanics
extracted.subtask_description: House style and notation rules for preparing manuscripts for the Journal of Fluid Mechanics, covering typography, mathematical notation, figures/tables, references, spelling, hyphenation and other editorial conventions authors must follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface for specific mathematical items
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a roman typeface in maths for: the d (or D) in differentials and integrals; i (square root of -1); e (exponential); units and abbreviations (but all sub- and superscripts, apart from those just listed, are italic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: d, i, e, physical units (cm, s), and abbreviations such as c.c. and h.o.t. should be upright roman. See section 5.2.1 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface for vectors, matrices and tensors
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the appropriate typeface for vectors, matrices and tensors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions: bold italic (or bold sloping greek) for vectors (including a bold nabla), bold sloping sans serif for tensors and matrices, and script as an alternative when the same letter denotes different quantities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Square-root notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Denote square roots by a fractional exponent rather than the root sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ( ... )^{1/2} not \sqrt{...}. See section 5.2.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation after equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Put punctuation after displayed equations where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displayed equations are part of the sentence and should be punctuated accordingly (period, comma, etc.). See §5.1 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid small in-line fractions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use small stacked fractions in running text except for simple numerals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In text use gh/u rather than \frac{gh}{u}. In displayed maths use gh/u or normal sized fractions; small fractions like \frac{1}{2} or \frac{2}{3} for numerals are acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters associated with numbers and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters (a, b, etc.) associated with equation numbers, figure or table numbers and references are italic, and for figures and tables are in brackets unless in a phrase already in brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: figure 1 (a), figure 1 (a--e), figures 1 (a) and 1 (b). See §§5.1, 3, 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use British spelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Use British spelling conforming to the Shorter Oxford English Dictionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: centre, behaviour, modelling, emphasise, analyse, zeroth, colour, travelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation and en-rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyphenate compound adjectives and use an en rule (double hyphen) for 'and' or 'to' and numeric ranges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: high-frequency wave, solid-body rotation; Navier--Stokes, pressure--strain, pages 45--56. Use hyphens after self-, cross-, half-; non- except nonlinear. Nouns with prefixes are normally one word unless repetition occurs (semi-infinite).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference list ordering and format
rubrics_metrics.description: References are listed at the end of the paper in strict alphabetical order. If the same author(s) has more than one publication in the same year, add a, b, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private communications are not included in References (mention in text with initials). Submitted or in-press articles may be included with full title and journal. Include thesis titles. Publisher addresses generally not needed (except University Presses). Conference proceedings must include editors and publisher. Follow JFM style and short journal-title conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: References in text formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: In-text references should include the author(s) name and the year in parentheses, unless the reference is already in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: see Smith (1989) or (see Smith 1989). Strings of references in parentheses separated by semicolons: (Jones 1967, 1978; Tam 1980; Dog 1991). Page/section numbers follow the date (Smith (1987, p. 234)). Three-author works: list all names at first mention, then use et al.; for four or more authors, use et al. from the start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title capitalization and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be simple and concise with only the first word capitalized (apart from proper names).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If paper is part of a series style as 'Annular flow. Part 3. Experiments'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors and affiliations formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors' names appear together on the same line, capitalized; addresses are listed separately below with superscript numerals if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postal addresses must be full including postal codes and country. New addresses can be indicated in a footnote to the author's name. 'Received' and 'revised' dates are added by Editorial Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract should be self-contained and self-explanatory and contain a summary of purpose, methodology, results and conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid references and displayed equations in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section heading style and symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the first word of a heading is capitalized (apart from proper names). In the text use the symbol § instead of the word 'section' (except at the start of a sentence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section headings are bold, so any maths symbols not normally bold (i.e. not vectors) should be changed to italic to match; see Input Guide for LaTeX handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements and dedications
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention any financial support in Acknowledgements; dedications are not normally permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledgements appear before appendices/references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices placement and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices appear between acknowledgements and references; long detailed appendices of interest to few readers are not printed but held in the Editorial Office and made available on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep appendices concise if intended for print.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures: submission and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures cannot currently be handled in electronic form so hard copies must be provided; include dummy vertical space with the caption in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour pictures are charged to the author. Figures must be numbered sequentially in order mentioned, each with a caption. Avoid large white space; put complicated information in the caption rather than on the figure; avoid duplicating information. Group similar figures as parts (a), (b) etc with a single caption. The word 'figure' is never abbreviated and only capitalized at sentence start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: numbering and numeric formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables must be numbered sequentially in the order mentioned, each having a caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use zeros before decimal points for numbers < 1 (e.g. 0.5), and prefer powers of 10 rather than 'e-4' notation. Extensive detailed tables of interest to few readers are held in the Editorial Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout of displayed equations
rubrics_metrics.description: Long, complicated or important equations are displayed and punctuated as part of the text. Numbered equations appear on separate lines; related equations may be labelled (2a), (2b) etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short related equations may be on same line separated by a space and numbered (2 a, b) style. Two or more equations on separate lines but with same number should be braced together. Displayed equations are centered; long ones should be broken before a + or - sign; use × if break is at a product. Words such as 'for', 'as' should be roman with an em space on each side. Small fractions should only be used for numerals; short simple fractions may be typed with a slash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing equations in text
rubrics_metrics.description: When referring to equations in the text, only the number in parentheses need be given; the word 'Equation' is only needed at the start of a sentence and should never be abbreviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using numerals in parentheses for any other reason. Non-displayed equations within the text must be short and simple, with fractions on one line only using a slash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multiletter symbols for variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid multiletter symbols (e.g. KE) for variables; use subscripts instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use E_K for kinetic energy. Dimensionless numbers like Re, Pr may be used, with smaller spacing between letters than normal math mode; see Input Guide for spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font choices for particular mathematical items
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify which kinds of mathematical items are upright (roman) versus italic or bold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Roman: mathematical operations (sin, log, d), constants (i, exp, e), Airy functions Ai, Bi, Re/Im (real/imag), physical units, and abbreviations (c.c., h.o.t.). Greek letters: slanted for variables; constants such as pi and mu and operators such as Δ are upright. Bold italic/bold sloping greek for vectors; bold sloping sans serif for tensors/matrices; script as alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product notation conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A symbol is not normally used to denote a product; use multiplication symbols only in specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use × when breaking displayed equations, for vector products, or between numbers (e.g. 106 × 10^4). Use a centered dot only for scalar products of vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of approximation symbols and order notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use ≈ to denote 'approximately equal to', ~ to denote 'asymptotically equal to', and O to denote 'of the order of'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these symbol conventions consistently for asymptotic/approximate expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units formatting and SI preference
rubrics_metrics.description: The International System of Units (SI) should normally be used; prefer exponents to a solidus and leave a space between number and units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: cm s^{-1}; write '5 and 6 cm' not '5cm and 6cm'. Use a low decimal point. Use % and ° symbols; on figures axis labels should be (deg.) rather than placing ° by each number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Only commonly accepted abbreviations may be used and they must be defined at first occurrence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use full stops between lower-case letters in abbreviations (e.g. e.g.), but not between capital letters. There is no point after some contractions (engng). Do not use the following abbreviations: 2-D, 3-D, l.h.s., r.h.s., fig., eq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spelling and capitalization conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use British spelling and initial capitals for proper names and their derivatives; do not capitalize figure, table, section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of proper-name capitals: Gaussian, Lagrangian, Cartesian, Pitot. Examples of British spellings: behaviour, analyse, travelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation and hyphenation detailed rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for hyphens, compound adjectives, prefixes, en rules and comma usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hyphenate compound adjectives before nouns (large-scale region) but not after ('equation of first order'). Self-, cross-, half- always followed by hyphen. 'non' usually hyphenated (non-linear except nonlinear). Compound nouns and prefixes normally one word unless repetition (semi-infinite). Use en rules (double hyphen) for replacing 'and' or 'to' (gravity--capillary). No comma after an abbreviating point (e.g. i.e. or cf.) and no comma between lists of adjectives. If a complete sentence is inside parentheses, include the final full stop inside.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid footnotes and separate nomenclature lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid footnotes since they interrupt reading; separate lists of nomenclature are not normally permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols should be defined and explained on first appearance in the text rather than via a separate nomenclature list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics
rubrics_metrics.description: Italics should seldom be used for emphasis but may be used in definitions and for foreign words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve italics for formal emphasis, definitions, or non-English words. Keep emphasis sparing.
